RESOLVED: PATCH /auth/me now accepts all 4 roles. Real scoping finding, not a simple permission swap: manager/admin/registered_user have no profile table in Postgres at all (location_manager.user_id is a bare Cognito sub, not a FK, by design) -- editing their name/phone would mean a Cognito-attribute edit from the frontend, not a backend DB write. Rather than inventing a table, non-owner roles now get an honest 404 (code: no_editable_profile) instead of a wrongful 403. Owner's write also now lazily provisions owner_account itself (previously a require_owner side effect). Also fixed in the same PR: update_me was writing zero audit_log entries -- a pre-existing violation of root CLAUDE.md's audit_log requirement, caught during self-review.

column8: Found live 2026-09-18 while testing scripts/delete_test_user.py: 3 consecutive 30s Lambda timeouts, zero app-level logs, while GET /cuisine-tags (no Cognito call) succeeded normally. Root cause: cognito-idp:ListUsers IAM permission existed since PR #10, but no NAT Gateway and no cognito-idp VPC endpoint ever existed -- find_sub_by_email() (manager assignment, seed_dev_data, bulk_import_restaurants, delete_user_data) has been unreachable from inside the Lambda in every real deployment, invisible because every test mocks the Cognito call. Fix: aws_vpc_endpoint.cognito_idp added to infra/modules/networking/main.tf, same pattern as the existing secretsmanager/logs endpoints (~$7.30/mo per AZ). Full writeup: docs/DECISIONS.md "Missing Cognito VPC endpoint". terraform validate passed in an isolated scratch copy; a human still needs to run terraform apply for this to take effect.

column1: Fix: session used wrong Cognito token type, blocking every real owner from provisioning
column8: SEVERE, found live 2026-09-18: LoginForm.tsx/sessionKeepAlive.ts captured the Cognito ACCESS token as the session credential, but access tokens carry no email claim -- auth_service.py's lazy owner_account provisioning needs one, so every real owner hit "An email claim is required to provision an owner account" on first login, platform-wide, since deployment. Fixed by switching to the ID token (same call sites, session.ts's CognitoJwtVerifier tokenUse updated to match) -- no Cognito reconfiguration needed, backend already accepted either token_use. Full writeup: docs/DECISIONS.md "Frontend used the wrong Cognito token type...". Also separately found+fixed same day: real Aurora DB was 3 Alembic migrations behind (photo_thumbnail_key, data_deletion_request, restaurant_brand_website) -- alembic_upgrade management command run to bring it current.
